text:
A Windows your apps recognize. 

Website and documentation

Raven runs Windows applications on Linux. You install them with their own installers, the same ones you would use on a PC, and they start: no virtual machine, no winetricks, no DLL overrides.

The program's code runs directly on your CPU, inside a sandbox where it cannot reach Linux. Every call it makes to the system is answered by Raven, which plays the part of the Windows kernel and its services: processes and threads, files, the registry, windows and input. Graphics go to Wayland and Vulkan, with DXVK and vkd3d-proton for Direct3D.

 Requirements

- Linux on x86 64
- CMake 3.20 or newer, a C++20 compiler and Python 3.11 or newer
- MinGW-w64 13 or newer for x86 64 and i686, to build the Windows test programs
- To build the installer components: clang, widl, bison and patch
- Optionally, OpenSSL for crypt32's certificate chains, Schannel, HTTPS and the CryptoAPI ciphers
- For desktop applications: Wayland, xkbcommon, pixman, FreeType and Vulkan
- Optionally, for the experimental X11 desktop: libxcb with its xkb, xfixes and xinput extensions, and xkbcommon-x11

The tested setup also uses libpng 1.6.59, a CPU build of Skia with the Liberation fonts, DXVK and vkd3d-proton; the scripts/provision- .py tools download the pinned versions.

 Installation

Raven is built from source for now:

 

Then run an installer, or any program:

 

This minimal build runs console programs and simple windows. Installers and most desktop programs also need the common controls, the shell dialogs and the installer services, which Raven builds from its own sources and, for the installer services, pinned upstream libraries, for both 64-bit and 32-bit programs. Without them a program stops at its first call into them, such as InitCommonControls :

 

DXVK and vkd3d-proton are only needed for Direct3D programs and games. The Microsoft root certificates let installers check the signatures of the packages they download, as setups built with WiX Burn and the .NET and Visual C++ redistributables do.

On an X11 session, --desktop=x11 takes the place of --desktop=wayland . The X11 desktop is experimental; -DRAVEN DESKTOP WAYLAND=OFF builds Raven without Wayland at all.

 RAVEN PREFIX is the Windows installation the program sees, with its own C: drive and registry. Programs installed in the same prefix see each other, as they would on one Windows machine; a separate prefix is only needed to keep a program fully apart from the others. Raven takes a snapshot of the prefix before every installer, and build/native/raven --restore-prefix brings it back. When the installer ends, what it made belongs to the program it installed; a program nothing installed is known by its executable, and owns the folder it runs from inside the prefix. Each program writes what it owns, and whatever it makes where nothing was, in place for every program to see; what it changes anywhere else in the prefix goes to a layer only it sees, which build/native/raven --discard-layer NAME or the control panel throws away ( --list-apps names the programs). The person's documents, the temporary folders and the registry keys Windows reads for every program, such as Run, Uninstall and file types, stay shared.

A program sees none of your Linux files except the ones you hand it: its own folder, the host paths on its command line, and what you choose in its file dialogs, which appear under Z: at their usual spelling. The file dialog runs apart from the program, sees your whole computer while you choose, and grants the program only the file or folder you chose. Anything else the program asks for is refused and noted in the prefix's sandbox.log .

The control panel ( control.exe in the prefix) manages all of it: the folders programs may open, network access for the prefix, the refusals, snapshots, and the Linux programs the prefix may hand files to. A Linux program you expose appears to Windows programs as C:\Program Files\Raven\Host\NAME.exe and receives only the files the calling program reaches; for each kind of file or address you choose a program of the prefix, a Linux program, or to be asked. The settings live in sandbox.conf in the prefix.

On kernels with Landlock, Raven also confines itself: it reaches only the prefix, its own files, the system's libraries and devices, and the paths granted to the program, and a small helper started before the confinement opens what is granted later.

To run the tests:

 

The display tests start a headless labwc in /run/user/ /raven-labwc-runtime , or raven-labwc-gpu for the hardware variants. Set RAVEN TEST RUNTIME to another directory to put them there, so that two runs on one machine do not share a compositor.

Some tests need software Raven cannot redistribute; point RAVEN MINESWEEPER , RAVEN NETFX INSTALLER , RAVEN NETFX35 PACKAGE , RAVEN XNA INSTALLER and RAVEN REDIST DIRECTORY at your own copies, or those tests are skipped. Each component under native/upstream records where it comes from and its license.

 What works today

 Area Status 
 --- --- 
 32 and 64-bit programs Both, side by side in the same prefix 
 Installers NSIS, Inno Setup and Windows Installer (MSI) packages, with custom actions, rollback and elevation 
 Visual C++ 2005 to 2022 x86 and x64, alone or all together, reinstalled, older over newer 
 .NET Framework 4.8 Installs from Microsoft's offline installer; console, WinForms and WPF programs run 
 .NET Framework 3.5 Enabled from its package as Windows does; CLR 2.0 programs run 
 DirectX June 2010, XNA 4.0, OpenAL Install from their official redistributables 
 Direct3D 8 and 9 Through DXVK, including 32-bit programs 
 Direct3D 11 Through DXVK: every shader stage, compute, MSAA, deferred contexts 
 Direct3D 12 Through vkd3d-proton, including ray tracing 
 Side-by-side assemblies Manifests, WinSxS and activation contexts

install.title: Installation
install.html:
Raven is built from source for now:

git clone https://github.com/mirkobrombin/raven.git
cd raven
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
cmake --build build -j2

Then run an installer, or any program:

export RAVEN_PREFIX="$HOME/.local/share/raven/my-app"
build/native/raven --run-process --execution=native --timeout-ms=600000 --desktop=wayland setup.exe

This minimal build runs console programs and simple windows. Installers and most desktop programs also need the common controls, the shell dialogs and the installer services, which Raven builds from its own sources and, for the installer services, pinned upstream libraries, for both 64-bit and 32-bit programs. Without them a program stops at its first call into them, such as InitCommonControls:

python3 scripts/provision-rtl.py --output components/rtl
python3 scripts/provision-controls.py --output components/controls
python3 scripts/provision-controls.py --arch x86 --output components/controls32
python3 scripts/provision-installer.py --output components/installer
python3 scripts/provision-installer.py --arch x86 --output components/installer32
python3 scripts/provision-graphics.py --destination components/graphics
python3 scripts/provision-roots.py --output components/roots
python3 scripts/provision-text.py --output components/text
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
    -DRAVEN_RTL_COMPONENT_PATH=$PWD/components/rtl/raven-rtl.dll \
    -DRAVEN_CONTROLS_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/controls -DRAVEN_CONTROLS32_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/controls32 \
    -DRAVEN_INSTALLER_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/installer -DRAVEN_INSTALLER32_COMPONENT_DIR=$PWD/components/installer32 \
    -DRAVEN_DXVK_PE64_DIR=$PWD/components/graphics/dxvk/pe64 -DRAVEN_DXVK_PE32_DIR=$PWD/components/graphics/dxvk/pe32 \
    -DRAVEN_VKD3D_PE64_DIR=$PWD/components/graphics/vkd3d-proton/pe64 \
    -DRAVEN_ROOT_CERTIFICATE_DIRECTORY=$PWD/components/roots \
    -DRAVEN_SKIA_SOURCE=$PWD/components/text/skia -DRAVEN_SKIA_LIBRARY=$PWD/components/text/cpu-fonts/libskia.a \
    -DRAVEN_FONT_DIRECTORY=$PWD/components/text/fonts
cmake --build build -j2

To run the tests:
